events.credibility_reason: Known only from talk abstracts and search snippets; no written proof located.

why: The statement is a universal claim over all 6-connected K6-minor-free graphs. The only post-snapshot event, the 2026 order-13 result, covers a single vertex count, which is a finite set of graphs, and the record says the argument is an exhaustive computer enumeration (nauty plus a minor search, 340 hours). That is a census of one finite instance-size, so I answered instances (F5) rather than case. The case reading turns on the large-N theorem leaving only finitely many orders. Even so, N is unstated and order 14 and above stay open, so the enumeration settles no infinite subclass. For consistency, the 2019 order-12 result is also instances. The large-graph, bounded-treewidth and girth-6 results restrict to infinite classes, so they are case results, each digested through JCTB or J. Combinatorics. The Norin–Thomas talk claim is a case result, unreviewed, and doubtful because no write-up exists. No AI system is named in any event; the 2026 paper's computer assistance is classical software.
doubts: The order-13 call between instances and case is close. If it were case, the problem would sit at partial with no AI involvement; the AI answer is none either way. The order-13 paper was read only through a summarising fetch of its HTML version.
